key_insight: Affine Memory Replay (AMR) uses continual learning with replayed and synthesized past simulations to keep molecular communication performance estimates accurate as experimental settings become more complex.
engineering_relevance: This enables reliable, incremental evaluation of bio-nanomachine communication protocols without retraining from scratch, supporting scalable design and testing of molecular communication systems.
method: Stores past simulation samples in memory
Generates replay samples by interpolation and extrapolation between past samples
Replays real and synthetic samples during sequential training to preserve earlier knowledge while learning new settings
evidence_signal: In incremental performance estimation tasks, AMR outperformed existing continual learning methods in overall accuracy while maintaining a balance between stability and plasticity under moderate training cost.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality and representativeness of stored samples and synthetic interpolation/extrapolation, which may be sensitive in highly non-linear or out-of-distribution settings.
paper_title: Continual Learning for Reliable In-Sequence Molecular Communication
